title: Understanding the Lucas Herrington Salary: Hourly to Annual Conversion Guide
description: Learn how to convert hourly rates to annual salary using the Lucas Herrington salary example. Includes National Minimum Wage, award rates, casual loading, tax, and super.
salarySummary: For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week at the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, the annual gross salary is approximately $52,229.44 before tax and super.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time role of 38 hours per week, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. For example, at the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, annual gross pay is $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,229.44. This assumes no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances.

faqs.q: What is casual loading and how does it affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an additional 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for lack of paid leave entitlements. For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is $26.44 × 1.25 = $33.05 per hour. When using our timesheet, you can check the 'casual loading' box to add this automatically. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading.

faqs.q: How is tax and super calculated on my annual salary?
faqs.a: Tax is calculated using the 2026–27 resident tax scale: nil on the first $18,200, 15% on income up to $45,000, 30% up to $135,000, 37% up to $190,000, and 45% above that. Medicare levy is generally 2%. Superannuation guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top of your salary, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For example, on a $52,229 salary, super would be about $6,267.48 per year.

bodyMarkdown:
## Introduction

If you’ve ever searched for “lucas herrington salary” online, you’ve probably seen a mix of figures from recruiter surveys, job boards, and official sources. The truth is that the most reliable pay data comes from the Fair Work Ombudsman and the Fair Work Commission. This guide will help you cut through the noise and understand exactly how to convert an hourly rate to an annual salary, whether you’re on the National Minimum Wage, an award rate, or a casual contract.

We’ll walk through the standard formula, explain the difference between minimum and award wages, cover casual loading, and show how tax and superannuation fit in. By the end, you’ll be able to confidently estimate your annual pay using the same method that underpins our [the timesheet](/) and [pay guides](/blog).

## The National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for a 38‑hour week. This is the legal floor for employees not covered by an award or enterprise agreement. However, most workers are covered by a modern award, which sets higher minimum rates for specific industries and roles. For example, the Children’s Services Award and Pharmacy Award have recently been updated following the Fair Work Commission’s gender‑based undervaluation review, as noted in the Modern Awards Pay Database.

The Fair Work Ombudsman publishes pay guides for each award, which include the minimum hourly rates, allowances, and penalty rates. You can find these on the Pay guides page. Always check the relevant award before relying on a single figure like “lucas herrington salary” from a non‑official source.

## Converting Hourly to Annual Salary

The standard formula is simple: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**. For a full‑time employee working 38 hours per week, this becomes:

**Annual gross salary = hourly rate × 38 × 52**

Let’s apply it to the National Minimum Wage:
- $26.44 × 38 = $1,004.72 per week (rounded to $1,004.90 in official figures)
- $1,004.72 × 52 = $52,245.44 per year (the official weekly figure gives $52,254.80)

If you’re paid fortnightly, simply multiply your weekly pay by 2. For the minimum wage, that’s $2,009.80 per fortnight.

This calculation assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. If your hours vary, you’ll need to average them over a longer period. Our [reference tables](/data) provide pre‑calculated conversions for common hourly rates.

## Understanding Casual Loading

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid sick leave or annual leave. For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is $26.44 × 1.25 = $33.05 per hour. When using our timesheet, you can check the “casual loading” box to add this automatically. **Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading** – the tool will apply it for you.

Award rates also have casual loadings, but they may be different. Always check the specific award. The Fair Work Commission’s Modern Awards Pay Database includes penalty rates and allowances for each classification, which can be downloaded as Excel spreadsheets.

## Tax and Super Considerations

Your annual gross salary is not what you take home. Tax and Medicare levy are deducted, and superannuation is paid on top by your employer.

**Tax (2026–27 resident scale):**
- $0 – $18,200: Nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% on excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30% on excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37% on excess over $135,000
- Over $190,000: 45% on excess over $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. For a full‑time minimum wage earner ($52,229), the tax would be approximately $5,092 plus Medicare of $1,045, leaving a take‑home of about $46,092. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool for a detailed estimate.

**Superannuation:** The super guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top of your salary. It is not deducted from your pay. For the example above, super would be $52,229 × 12% = $6,267.48 per year, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for more.

## Using the Pay Guides and Modern Awards Database

When you search for “lucas herrington salary” or any specific role, the most accurate figures come from the Fair Work Ombudsman’s Pay and Conditions Tool and the Fair Work Commission’s Modern Awards Pay Database. These are updated after each Annual Wage Review and include all legal minimums.

The Pay guides page lists minimum rates for every award, while the database provides detailed spreadsheets of classifications, allowances, and penalty rates. Always cross‑check any third‑party salary figure against these official sources.

## Conclusion

Converting an hourly rate to an annual salary is straightforward once you know the hours and any loadings. The key is to use authoritative data from the Fair Work Ombudsman and Fair Work Commission rather than relying on generic search results like “lucas herrington salary”. Remember that your actual pay may differ due to overtime, allowances, or enterprise agreements. Use our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool to run your own numbers, and always consult the relevant award or pay guide for your industry.
